chunks: From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most beloved of deeds to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is causing gladness to enter upon the believers.'
ai.seo_question: What is considered the most beloved deed to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to emphasize that alleviating the distress of a believer is not merely a social courtesy but a direct path to divine pleasure, a concept central to Shia ethics of *mu'amalat*. This act is often interpreted by scholars as a means of expiating sins and strengthening the communal bond (*ta'awun*) among the faithful, reflecting the Prophet's love for his community. It underscores the Shia view that spiritual merit is deeply intertwined with social responsibility and emotional care for others.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Abu Ali, from Abu Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The most Beloved of the deeds to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is causing the gladness to enter upon the Momineen’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Bakr ibn Salih from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim from Ali ibn abu Ali from abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following:
‘‘The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Of the most beloved deed to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, is bringing joy to the heart of the believer.’”
